title: Bendix Field Engineering as a CIA non-official cover front

tellings.quote: the field engineering division was legendary to us because number one they had very good field engineers but number two the real reason is they were a front when CIA or somebody wanted to send somebody abroad under cover as a knock you know nonofficial cover they would use Bendix field engineering services

plain: Peter Levenda, a writer billed on the show as a CIA historian, says that in the 1970s the field engineering division of the Bendix company in Manhattan was used by the CIA as a front to send officers abroad under "non-official cover", meaning posing as private employees rather than as government staff. Levenda tells Michels this from his own time around the company: the division was "legendary to us" because "when CIA or somebody wanted to send somebody abroad under cover" they used Bendix field engineering. If true, a regular engineering firm doubled as a cover for spies.
